summary: You follow one of two pathways, at least six courses and 24 units either way. The traditional pathway (no subplan) is SOC 1 or 170, one of SOC 2, 180A or 180B, two foundation courses and two more Sociology courses. The Poverty, Inequality, and Policy subplan is SOC 3 and a second core course, breadth courses in two areas and two electives (one may be the SOC 192 research apprenticeship). S and CR grades count; a course taken for a letter grade needs a C or better. Substitutions the Director of Undergraduate Studies approves are moved in by hand.

lHmgdlFp.why: "Students required to complete 2 courses from 2 different categories." Each category is one course, so "Inequality and Mobility" is one of its five courses, not all of them.

P4lr3PPY.why: "Choose two electives ... students may petition for approval of other courses related to inequality, poverty, and mobility. Students may also elect to take additional elective courses from any of the breadth areas above." Research apprenticeship: "Students may replace one elective with a research apprenticeship" (SOC 192, at most one).

OSW0nj1b.why: "Optional Research Apprenticeship (up to five units) ... Students may replace one elective with a research apprenticeship". Not required: SOC 192 is now one of the electives, at most one.

program.why: Grading: "Grades of 'S' or 'CR' are allowable. When students take classes for a letter grade, a grade of 'C' or better should be earned or the student should obtain a written exception."

totals.label: Six courses
totals.why: Policies: "24 units of sociology coursework (or 6 classes, whichever is greater) are required for the sociology minor."

add.why: Policies: "Related coursework from other departments may fulfill a minor requirement. All course substitutions must be approved by the Sociology Director of Undergraduate Studies."

rIbgVFqI.why: Overview: "There is one Sociology minor, which offers two pathways for students to choose from: The traditional minor pathway, which follows the requirements listed in 'Program Requirements'. The subplan in Poverty, Inequality, and Policy". The Program Requirements are the traditional pathway, so a student in the subplan does not also take them.
